scoring_justification: Recompute f0 and chi_eff from raw force-velocity CSV via linear regression and compare to paper values with tolerances; detect velocity peaks from CSV; validate shape of output files.

hidden_assets.purpose: Interface area A_i and van der Waals separation h_vdW for computing mu_eff
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Derived from paper's Eq.(2) using mu_eff=0.27 cP, chi_eff=2.3, assuming typical h_vdW=3.4 Å
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Consistent with paper's reported effective viscosity and force-velocity relation, allowing verification of derived property.

outputs.description: Time series of applied force and NT axial velocity, from which the checker recomputes f0 and χeff.
Agent-reported fitted parameters; the checker compares these to hidden reference values.
Velocity peaks detected after step 141,000, verifying the discrete acceleration events reported in the paper.

output_contract.notes: All output files must be placed in /app/outputs. The checker will recompute f0 and χeff from force_velocity_data.csv and compare against paper values within tolerances. The velocity peaks will be checked for correct timing and minimum magnitude.

steps.description: Validate CSV shape: required columns, non-empty rows.
Check fitted_parameters.json exists and contains required keys.
Check velocity_peaks.json is a non-empty array of objects with step and velocity_A_per_ps.
Recompute f0, χeff from force-velocity CSV via linear regression; compute μeff using hidden A_i and h_vdW; score each within tolerance.
Detect velocity peaks after step 141000 in CSV; require at least 2 peaks with velocity > 0.5 Å/ps.
